Package manager service modifications
Unable to connect to Xposed service
Make sure the Xposed framework is running and this module is enabled.
Bypass downgrade
Bypass verification
Bypass digest
Bypass exact signature match
Use previous signatures
Bypass shared user verification
Disable Package Verification Agent
Allow installing an older version over a newer version.
Allow installing APKs with invalid or modified signatures.
Bypass resources.arsc alignment restriction
Allow installing APKs whose resources.arsc is compressed or not 4-byte aligned on Android 11 and later.
Allow reinstalling an app with a different signature.
Allow split APKs to use different signatures.
Always use the installed app\'s signatures during installation.
Any APK may overwrite the installed app. Enable only when necessary.
Allow hidden APIs for system apps
Allow system apps with signatures that do not match the platform signature to use hidden APIs without restriction.
Xiaomi/Redmi users must not enable this option; otherwise, the device may fail to boot.
Allow packages with a different shared-user signature.
For example, Google Play Protect.
Bypass installation blocklist
Bypass blocklists on devices such as Nothing Phone.
Bypass duplicate permission declarations
Allow packages with a different signature (e.g. a cloned app) to redefine a custom permission already owned by another package.
Any installed app may redefine a permission already declared by another app, which can let it receive broadcasts or access components intended only for the original owner. Enable only when necessary.
Bypass duplicate provider declarations
Allow packages with a different signature (e.g. a cloned app) to declare a content provider authority already used by another package.
Any installed app may claim a content provider authority already used by another app, which can let it intercept content:// requests meant for the original owner. Enable only when necessary.
Also rename sensitive providers (e.g. FileProvider)
When a duplicate authority belongs to a provider like FileProvider, whose authority is usually hardcoded elsewhere in the app\'s own code, rename it too instead of leaving it alone.

FileProvider-style authorities are often referenced directly in app code (e.g. to share files). Renaming them lets installation succeed, but any such code path that still points at the old authority may silently fail or reach the wrong app. Only enable this if you understand the tradeoff.
